translations.literal: Tang Zong
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zong

sentences.zh: 郁新，字敦本，臨淮人。

translations.literal: Yu Xin, styled Dunben, was a native of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xin, whose style name was Dunben, came from Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，以人才征，授戶部度支主事。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign he was summoned for his talent and appointed Director of Expenditures in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongwu era he was recruited for ability and made Director of Expenditures in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the post of director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 逾年，擢本部右侍郎。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was elevated to Right Vice Minister of the same ministry.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was raised to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 嘗問天下戶口田賦，地理險易，應答無遺，帝稱其才。

translations.literal: He was once asked about the empire's household registers, land tax, and the strategic strengths and weaknesses of geography, and answered without omission; the emperor praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: When questioned on national population registers, land taxes, and the strategic lay of the realm, he answered exhaustively, and the emperor commended his talent.

sentences.zh: 尋進尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was advanced to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時親王歲祿米五萬石，新定議減五之四，並定郡王以下祿有差。

translations.literal: At that time princes of the blood received fifty thousand piculs of grain per year as stipend; Xin newly fixed a policy reducing this by four-fifths, and also fixed graded stipends for commandery princes and below.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, imperial princes drew fifty thousand piculs of grain a year; Xin drew up a plan to cut that by four-fifths and set graded stipends for commandery princes and those of lower rank.

sentences.zh: 又以邊餉不繼，定召商開中法，令商輸粟塞下，按引支鹽，邊儲以足。

translations.literal: Because frontier provisions were not continuous, he established the policy of summoning merchants to open the zhongfa salt franchise, ordering merchants to deliver grain below the passes and receive salt by certificate, so that frontier stores were made sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: When frontier supplies ran short, he instituted the merchant zhongfa system: merchants delivered grain to the border and drew salt by certificate, and frontier granaries were filled.

sentences.zh: 夏原吉為戶部主事，新重之，諸曹事悉委任焉。

translations.literal: Xia Yuanji served as a director in the Ministry of Revenue; Xin valued him and entrusted him with all affairs of the various bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji was a director in the ministry; Xin held him in high regard and delegated every bureau matter to him.

sentences.zh: 建文二年引疾歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Jianwen reign he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwen 2 he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，召掌戶部事，以古樸為侍郎佐之。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, Xin was summoned to manage the Ministry of Revenue, with Gu Pu as vice minister to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongle Emperor's accession, Xin was called to head the Ministry of Revenue, with Gu Pu as vice minister to aid him.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，河南蝗，有司不以聞，新劾治之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle, locusts struck Henan; the local officials did not report it, and Xin impeached and punished them.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1, locusts ravaged Henan; when officials failed to report it, Xin had them investigated and punished.

sentences.zh: 初，轉漕北京，新言：「自淮抵河，多淺灘跌坡，運舟艱阻。

translations.literal: Earlier, in turning transport to Beijing, Xin said: 'From the Huai to the Yellow River there are many shoals and steep drops, and transport vessels face hardship.
translations.idiomatic: When grain transport to Beijing was first organized, Xin said: 'From the Huai to the river route there are many shoals and steep drops, and the convoys are badly hindered.

sentences.zh: 請別用淺船載三百石者，自淮河、沙河運至陳州潁溪口跌坡下，復用淺船載二百石者運至跌坡上，別用大船運入黃河。

translations.literal: He asked that shallow boats of three hundred piculs be used separately to carry from the Huai and Sha rivers to below the drop at Chenzhou and the mouth of the Ying Stream, then shallow boats of two hundred piculs to carry above the drop, and then large boats to enter the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed shallow boats of three hundred piculs from the Huai and Sha rivers to below the Chenzhou–Ying Stream drop, then two-hundred-picul shallow boats above the drop, and large boats only for the Yellow River leg.

sentences.zh: 至八柳樹諸處，令河南車夫陸運入衛河，轉輸北京。」

translations.literal: At places such as Baliu Tree, he had Henan cart drivers transport overland into the Wei Canal and then forward to Beijing.'
translations.idiomatic: From Baliu Tree and similar points, Henan carters would haul grain overland into the Wei Canal for delivery to Beijing.'

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 又言：「湖廣屯田所產不一，請皆得輸官。

translations.literal: He also said: 'The produce of Huguang garrison fields is not uniform; I ask that all may be delivered to the government.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'Huguang garrison fields yield uneven crops; let every kind be accepted at the granary.

sentences.zh: 粟谷、縻黍、大麥、蕎穄二石，準米一石。

translations.literal: Two piculs of millet grain, glutinous millet, barley, or buckwheat were to count as one picul of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Two piculs of millet, glutinous millet, barley, or buckwheat would equal one picul of rice.

sentences.zh: 稻谷、秫二石五鬥，穇稗三石，各準米一石。

translations.literal: Two piculs and five dou of paddy or sorghum, or three piculs of barnyard millet or broomcorn, each counted as one picul of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Paddy or sorghum at two and a half piculs, or barnyard millet and broomcorn at three piculs, would each count as one picul of rice.

sentences.zh: 豆、麥、芝麻與米等。」

translations.literal: Beans, wheat, and sesame were equal to rice.'
translations.idiomatic: Beans, wheat, and sesame were rated equal to rice.'

sentences.zh: 著為令。

translations.literal: This was enacted as an ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: This was promulgated as law.

sentences.zh: 二年，議公、侯、伯、駙馬、儀賓祿，二百石以上者，請如文武官例，米鈔兼給。

translations.literal: In the second year, in deliberating the stipends of dukes, marquises, earls, imperial sons-in-law, and ceremonial sons-in-law, for those above two hundred piculs he asked that they follow the civil and military official precedent of mixed grain and paper money.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 2, when stipends for dukes, marquises, earls, imperial sons-in-law, and ceremonial sons-in-law were discussed, he proposed that those above two hundred piculs receive grain and paper money as civil and military officials did.

sentences.zh: 三年，以士卒勞困，議減屯田歲收不如額者十之四五，又議改納米北京贖罪者於南京倉。

translations.literal: In the third year, because soldiers and laborers were weary, he proposed reducing by four or five tenths the annual garrison harvest that fell short of quota, and also proposed shifting grain paid in Beijing to redeem crimes to the Nanjing granary.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, citing the exhaustion of troops and laborers, he proposed cutting shortfall garrison harvests by forty to fifty percent and moving grain-for-clemency payments from Beijing to the Nanjing granary.

sentences.zh: 皆允行。

translations.literal: All were approved and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 是年八月卒於官。

translations.literal: That year in the eighth month he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office that August.

sentences.zh: 帝嘆曰：「新理邦賦十三年，量計出入，今誰可代者？」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said: 'Xin managed the state's revenue for thirteen years, measuring income and outgo—who can replace him now?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lamented: 'Xin has managed the realm's revenue for thirteen years, balancing every intake and outlay—who can take his place?'

sentences.zh: 輟朝一日，賜葬祭，而召夏原吉還理部事。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for one day, burial rites were granted, and Xia Yuanji was summoned back to manage the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Court was halted for a day, burial honors were granted, and Xia Yuanji was recalled to run the ministry.

sentences.zh: 新長於綜理，密而不繁。

translations.literal: Xin excelled at comprehensive administration, thorough yet not cumbersome.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was skilled at overall management—meticulous without being burdensome.

sentences.zh: 其所規畫，後不能易。

translations.literal: The plans he laid down could not afterward be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing he designed was later overturned.

sentences.zh: 趙羾，字雲翰，夏人，徙祥符。

translations.literal: Zhao Gong, styled Yunhan, was a native of Xia who moved to Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gong, styled Yunhan, was of Xia descent and had settled in Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，由鄉舉入太學，授兵部職方司主事。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign he entered the Imperial Academy through the local examination and was appointed Registrar of the Bureau of Operations in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu he entered the Imperial Academy via the local examination and became Registrar of the Bureau of Operations in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 圖天下要害厄塞，並屯戍所宜以進。

translations.literal: He mapped the empire's strategic passes and choke points, together with where garrisons should be posted, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He charted the realm's critical passes and strongpoints, with recommended garrison placements, and submitted the maps.

sentences.zh: 帝以為才，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded him as talented and transferred him to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged him capable and promoted him to vice director.

sentences.zh: 建文初，遷浙江參政，建策捕海寇，有功。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign he was moved to Zhejiang as Administration Vice Commissioner; he devised plans to capture sea pirates and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianwen he became Zhejiang Administration Vice Commissioner, devised measures against sea pirates, and earned merit.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年，使交阯，還奏稱旨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle he was sent as envoy to Jiaozhi; on his return his memorial pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 2 he was envoy to Jiaozhi; his report on return pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 擢刑部侍郎，改工部，再改禮部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments, then transferred to Works, and again to Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of Punishments, then Works, then Rites.

sentences.zh: 五年進尚書，賜宴華蓋殿，撤膳羞遺其母。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was advanced to Minister; a banquet was given in the Hall of the Canopy of Flowers, and when the feast was cleared he sent the delicacies to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he became Minister and was feasted in the Hall of the Canopy of Flowers; when the table was cleared he sent the dishes home to his mother.

sentences.zh: 初，羾每以事為言者所劾，帝不問。

translations.literal: Earlier, whenever Gong was impeached by remonstrators over some matter, the emperor did not inquire into it.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, censors had often impeached Gong over one matter or another, but the emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 九年秋，朝鮮使臣將歸，例有賜賚，羾不以奏。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year, when Korean envoys were about to return, gifts were customarily bestowed, but Gong did not memorialize about it.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the ninth year, Korean envoys were leaving and customary gifts were due, but Gong filed no memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「是且使朕失遠人心。」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: 'This will make me lose the hearts of distant peoples.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged: 'This would make me lose the goodwill of distant states.'

sentences.zh: 遂下之獄。

translations.literal: He was thereupon imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 尋得釋，使督建隆慶、保安、永寧諸州縣，撫綏新集，民安其業。

translations.literal: Soon he was released and sent to supervise the building of the prefectures and counties of Longqing, Bao'an, and Yongning; he pacified the newly settled population, and the people were secure in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon freed and sent to oversee construction in Longqing, Bao'an, and Yongning; he soothed the new settlers and the people settled into their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 十五年丁母艱。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he observed mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 起復，改兵部尚書，專理塞外兵事。

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning, he was changed to Minister of War and devoted himself to frontier military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Called back from mourning, he was made Minister of War and charged solely with frontier military affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝北征，轉餉有方。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned north, Gong transferred provisions with method.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's northern campaigns, Gong organized supply transport with notable efficiency.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嗣位，改南京刑部。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor succeeded, Gong was transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Renzong Emperor he was moved to the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，御史張楷劾羾及侍郎俞士吉怠縱。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande, Censor Zhang Kai impeached Gong and Vice Minister Yu Shiji for negligence and indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 5, Censor Zhang Kai accused Gong and Vice Minister Yu Shiji of laxity and neglect.

sentences.zh: 召至，命致仕。

translations.literal: When summoned, he was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 羾性精敏，歷事五朝，位列卿，自奉如寒素。

translations.literal: Gong was by nature keen and precise; he served five reigns and stood among ministers, yet maintained himself like a poor scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was sharp and meticulous; he served five reigns and held ministerial rank, yet lived as frugally as a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 正統元年卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhengtong 1 at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 金忠，鄞人。

translations.literal: Jin Zhong was a native of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhong came from Yin.

sentences.zh: 少讀書，善《易》卜。

translations.literal: In youth he studied books and was skilled in divination by the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied the classics and was adept at Yijing divination.

sentences.zh: 兄戍通州亡，忠補戍。

translations.literal: His elder brother was garrisoned at Tongzhou and died; Zhong took his place in the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother had been posted to Tongzhou and died there; Zhong took his place as a garrison soldier.

sentences.zh: 貧不能行，相者袁珙資之。

translations.literal: Too poor to travel, he was financed by the physiognomist Yuan Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to make the journey, he was funded by the physiognomist Yuan Gong.

sentences.zh: 既至，編卒伍。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he was enrolled in the ranks of soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was enrolled in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 賣卜北平市，多中。

translations.literal: He practiced divination in the markets of Beiping and was often right.
translations.idiomatic: He told fortunes in the Beiping markets and was often accurate.

sentences.zh: 市人傳以為神。

translations.literal: The townspeople spread word that he was divine.
translations.idiomatic: Market folk spread tales that he was uncanny.

sentences.zh: 僧道衍稱於成祖。

translations.literal: The monk Daoyan praised him to the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Daoyan commended him to the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 成祖將起兵，托疾召忠卜，得鑄印乘軒之卦。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan was about to raise troops, he feigned illness and summoned Zhong to divine; he obtained the hexagram of casting a seal and riding in a carriage.
translations.idiomatic: As the Prince of Yan prepared to rise in arms, he feigned illness and had Zhong cast the hexagram; the reading was 'casting the seal and mounting the carriage.'

sentences.zh: 曰：「此象貴不可言。」

translations.literal: He said: 'This image is nobility beyond words.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said: 'This omen speaks of rank beyond words.'

sentences.zh: 自是出入燕府中，常以所占勸舉大事。

translations.literal: From then on he went in and out of the Yan mansion, and often used his divinations to urge undertaking the great affair.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he frequented the Yan mansion and repeatedly urged the great enterprise on the strength of his readings.

sentences.zh: 成祖深信之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan trusted him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The prince came to trust him utterly.

sentences.zh: 燕兵起，自署官屬，授忠王府紀善，守通州。

translations.literal: When the Yan army rose, he himself appointed officials, made Zhong Recorder of the princely establishment, and left him to hold Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan forces rose, the prince appointed his own staff, made Zhong Recorder of the princely establishment, and left him to defend Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 南兵數攻城不克。

translations.literal: The southern army repeatedly attacked the city but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Southern forces besieged the city again and again without success.

sentences.zh: 已，召置左右，有疑輒問，術益驗，且時進謀畫。

translations.literal: Afterward he was summoned to attend at the prince's side; whenever there was doubt he was asked, his art grew ever more verified, and he also offered stratagems from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was called to the prince's side; doubts were put to him at once, his divinations proved ever more reliable, and he offered counsel as well.

sentences.zh: 遂拜右長史，贊戎務，為謀臣矣。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Right Chief Clerk, assisted in military affairs, and became a strategist.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Chief Clerk, assisted in military affairs, and became a trusted strategist.

sentences.zh: 成祖稱帝，論佐命功，擢工部右侍郎，贊世子守北京。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan declared himself emperor, in assessing merit for aiding the founding he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Works and assisted the heir apparent in guarding Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became emperor, Zhong was rewarded for founding service with the post of Right Vice Minister of Works and was left to help the heir apparent hold Beijing.

sentences.zh: 尋召還，進兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled and advanced to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 帝起兵時，次子高煦從戰有功，許以為太子。

translations.literal: When the emperor first raised troops, his second son Gaoxu had followed the campaigns with merit and had been promised the position of heir.
translations.idiomatic: During the rebellion the emperor's second son, Gaoxu, had fought with distinction and been promised the heirship.

sentences.zh: 至是，淇國公邱福等黨高煦，勸帝立之。

translations.literal: At this time the Duke of Qi, Qiu Fu, and others formed a faction for Gaoxu and urged the emperor to install him.
translations.idiomatic: Now Qiu Fu, Duke of Qi, and others backed Gaoxu and pressed the emperor to name him heir.

sentences.zh: 獨忠以為不可，在帝前歷數古嫡孽事。

translations.literal: Zhong alone held it impossible and before the emperor enumerated ancient cases of legitimate and illegitimate succession.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhong objected, and before the throne he cited one after another the disasters of displacing the legitimate heir.

sentences.zh: 帝不能奪，密以告解縉、黃淮、尹昌隆。

translations.literal: The emperor could not prevail and secretly told Xie Jin, Huang Huai, and Yin Changlong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not override him and secretly informed Xie Jin, Huang Huai, and Yin Changlong.

sentences.zh: 縉等皆以忠言為是。

translations.literal: Jin and the others all held Zhong's words correct.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and the others all agreed with Zhong.

sentences.zh: 於是立世子為皇太子，而忠為東宮輔導官，以兵部尚書兼詹事府詹事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the heir apparent was established as crown prince, while Zhong became an instructor of the Eastern Palace, serving concurrently as Minister of War and Grand Mentor of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent was then named crown prince; Zhong became an Eastern Palace instructor, holding concurrently the posts of Minister of War and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 六年命兼輔皇太孫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered also to assist the imperial great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was also charged with tutoring the imperial great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 帝北征，留忠與蹇義、黃淮、楊士奇輔太子監國。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned north, he left Zhong with Jian Yi, Huang Huai, and Yang Shiqi to assist the crown prince in governing the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern campaign the emperor left Zhong with Jian Yi, Huang Huai, and Yang Shiqi to help the crown prince govern.

sentences.zh: 是時高煦奪嫡謀愈急，蜚語譖太子。

translations.literal: At this time Gaoxu's plot to seize the succession grew ever more urgent, and slanderous rumors defamed the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: By then Gaoxu's bid for the succession had grown desperate, and whispered calumnies assailed the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 十二年北征還，悉征東宮官屬下獄。

translations.literal: When the northern campaign returned in the twelfth year, all the Eastern Palace staff were summoned and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, after the northern campaign, every Eastern Palace officer was arrested.

sentences.zh: 以忠勛舊不問，而密令審察太子事。

translations.literal: Because of Zhong's founding merit he was not questioned, but he was secretly ordered to investigate the crown prince's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was spared on account of his founding merit, but secretly ordered to investigate the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 忠言無有。

translations.literal: Zhong reported that there was nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong reported nothing amiss.

sentences.zh: 帝怒。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 忠免冠頓首流涕，願連坐以保之。

translations.literal: Zhong removed his cap, bowed his head to the ground, and wept, wishing to be punished together with the crown prince in order to protect him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong doffed his cap, kowtowed with tears, and offered to share punishment in order to shield the heir.

sentences.zh: 以故太子得無廢，而宮僚黃淮、楊溥等亦以是獲全。

translations.literal: For this reason the crown prince was not deposed, and the palace staff Huang Huai, Yang Pu, and others also thereby escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the crown prince was not deposed, and palace officers such as Huang Huai and Yang Pu were spared as well.

sentences.zh: 忠起卒伍至大位，甚見親倚，每承顧問，知無不言，然慎密不泄。

translations.literal: Zhong had risen from the ranks of soldiers to high position and was greatly trusted and relied upon; whenever he received the emperor's attention he spoke without reserve, yet he was cautious and secret and did not leak.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from the ranks to high office, Zhong enjoyed the emperor's deep trust; on every audience he spoke frankly, yet he was discreet and revealed nothing.

sentences.zh: 處僚友不持兩端，退恒推讓之。

translations.literal: In dealing with colleagues he did not take two sides; in retirement he always yielded precedence.
translations.idiomatic: Among colleagues he never played both sides; in private he always deferred to others.

sentences.zh: 明年四月卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following April.

sentences.zh: 給驛歸葬，命有司治祠墓，復其家。

translations.literal: A courier station was provided for his burial return, officials were ordered to tend his shrine tomb, and his household was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Courier service was granted for his funeral journey, officials were told to maintain his tomb shrine, and his family was restored to favor.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年，追贈榮祿大夫少師，謚忠襄。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Mentor of the Palace with the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with the posthumous name Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongxi 1 he was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Palace with the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and the posthumous name Zhongxiang.

sentences.zh: 官子達翰林檢討。

translations.literal: His son Da was appointed Hanlin Academician Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Da was made a Hanlin Academician Expositor.

sentences.zh: 達剛直敢言，仕至長蘆都轉運使。

translations.literal: Da was upright and daring in speech, and in office rose to Salt Transport Commissioner of Changlu.
translations.idiomatic: Da was forthright and outspoken and rose to Salt Transport Commissioner of Changlu.

sentences.zh: 忠有兄華，負誌節。

translations.literal: Zhong had an elder brother Hua, who possessed integrity of purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhong had an elder brother, Hua, who was a man of firm principle.

sentences.zh: 忠守通州有功，欲推恩官之，辭不就。

translations.literal: Because Zhong's defense of Tongzhou had merit, the court wished to extend favor and appoint Hua to office, but he declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the court wished to reward Hua for Zhong's defense of Tongzhou, he refused office.

sentences.zh: 嘗召賜金綺，亦不受。

translations.literal: He was once summoned and granted brocade and silk, but he also would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Even when summoned and given brocade and silk, he would not take them.

sentences.zh: 成祖目為迂叟，放還。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor regarded him as an old pedant and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor called him a stubborn old fellow and let him go home.

sentences.zh: 一日，讀《宋史》至王倫附秦檜事，放聲長嘆而逝。

translations.literal: One day, reading the Song History to the affair of Wang Lun attaching himself to Qin Hui, he gave a loud long sigh and died.
translations.idiomatic: One day, reading in the Song History how Wang Lun sided with Qin Hui, he sighed aloud and died.

sentences.zh: 里中稱為「白雲先生」。

translations.literal: The neighborhood called him 'Master White Cloud.'
translations.idiomatic: His neighbors called him "Master of White Cloud".

sentences.zh: 李慶，字德孚，順義人。

translations.literal: Li Qing, styled Defu, was a native of Shunyi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qing, styled Defu, came from Shunyi.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，以國子生署右僉都御史，後授刑部員外郎，遷紹興知府。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign, as a student of the Imperial Academy he acted as Right Vice Censor-in-chief, later was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments, and transferred to prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, as an academy student he acted as Right Vice Censor-in-chief, later became Punishments vice director, then prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年召為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle he was summoned as Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1 he was summoned as Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 性剛果，有幹局，馭下甚嚴。

translations.literal: His nature was firm and decisive; he had executive ability and governed subordinates very strictly.
translations.idiomatic: He was firm and decisive, capable in administration, and governed subordinates very strictly.

sentences.zh: 帝以為才，數命治他事，不得時至部。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded him as talented and repeatedly ordered him to handle other affairs, so he could not always reach his ministry on time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regarded him as talented and often sent him on other duties, so he could not always attend his ministry.

sentences.zh: 然屬吏與罪人交通私饋餉，慶輒知之，繩以重法。

translations.literal: Yet when subordinate officials trafficked privately with criminals, Qing always knew and punished them by severe law.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when subordinates dealt privately with criminals, Qing always found out and punished them severely.

sentences.zh: 五年，改左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made Left Vice Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he became Left Vice Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 兩遭親喪，並起復。

translations.literal: He twice met parental mourning and both times was recalled from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He twice mourned parents and both times was recalled from mourning.

sentences.zh: 時勛貴武臣多令子弟家人行商中鹽，為官民害。

translations.literal: At the time meritorious nobles and military officers often had sons, younger relatives, and household members trade in monopoly salt, harming officials and people alike.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious nobles and military officers often had kin trade in monopoly salt, harming officials and people alike.

sentences.zh: 慶言：「舊制，四品以上官員家不得與民爭利。

translations.literal: Qing said: "Under the old system, households of officials of the fourth rank and above must not compete with the people for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Qing said: "Under the old system, households of officials of the fourth rank and above must not compete with the people for profit.

sentences.zh: 今都督蔡福等既行罰，公侯有犯，亦乞按問。」

translations.literal: Now that Commanders-in-Chief Cai Fu and others have already been punished, if dukes and marquises offend, I also ask that they be investigated."
translations.idiomatic: Now that Commanders-in-Chief Cai Fu and others have already been punished, if dukes and marquises offend, I also ask that they be investigated."

sentences.zh: 帝命嚴禁如制。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered strict prohibition according to the system.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered strict enforcement of the rule.

sentences.zh: 忻成伯趙彜擅殺運夫，盜賣軍餉。

translations.literal: Marquis of Xincheng Zhao Yi killed transport laborers on his own authority and stole and sold army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Xincheng Zhao Yi killed transport laborers on his own authority and stole and sold army provisions.

sentences.zh: 都督譚青、朱崇貪縱。

translations.literal: Commanders-in-Chief Tan Qing and Zhu Chong were greedy and indulgent.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders-in-Chief Tan Qing and Zhu Chong were greedy and indulgent.

sentences.zh: 慶劾之，皆下吏。

translations.literal: Qing impeached them, and all were sent down to the officials for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Qing impeached them, and all were sent to the courts.

sentences.zh: 已，劾都督費瓛欺罔、梁銘貪暴、鎮守德州都督曹得黷貨。

translations.literal: Later he impeached Commander-in-Chief Fei Huan for deception, Liang Ming for greedy violence, and Cao De, Commander-in-Chief defending Dezhou, for corrupt gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Later he impeached Commander-in-Chief Fei Huan for deception, Liang Ming for greed and violence, and Dezhou garrison commander Cao De for taking bribes.

sentences.zh: 皆被責。

translations.literal: All were punished.
translations.idiomatic: All were punished.

sentences.zh: 中外凜其風采。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court they stood in awe of his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the court they stood in awe of his bearing.

sentences.zh: 十八年進工部尚書，尋兼領兵部事。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was advanced to Minister of Works and soon also managed War affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he became Minister of Works and soon also headed War affairs.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，改兵部，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor took the throne, Li Qing was transferred to the Ministry of War and made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong Emperor succeeded, Li Qing was moved to the Ministry of War and made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 弋謙以言事忤旨，呂震等交口詆之，惟慶與夏原吉無所言。

translations.literal: Yi Qian offended the emperor by remonstrance; Lü Zhen and others all joined in denouncing him, but only Qing and Xia Yuanji said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi Qian offended the throne by speaking out, Lü Zhen and others denounced him in concert, but only Li Qing and Xia Yuanji held their tongues.

sentences.zh: 帝尋悟，降敕自責，並責震等，震等甚愧此兩人。

translations.literal: The emperor soon understood, issued an edict blaming himself, and also blamed Zhen and the others; Zhen and the others were deeply ashamed before these two men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon saw his error, issued a self-rebuke, and rebuked Zhen and the rest; they were deeply shamed before Qing and Xia.

sentences.zh: 山陵事多，趣辦中官有求，執不與，人多嚴憚之，號為「生李」。

translations.literal: With many matters of the imperial tomb to be hurried, eunuchs in charge of procurement made demands, but he firmly refused to grant them; many feared him and called him 'Living Li.'
translations.idiomatic: Tomb works pressed hard and palace eunuchs demanded favors, but he would not yield; people feared him and called him 'Living Li.'

sentences.zh: 奉命侍皇太子謁孝陵，在途約束將士，秋毫無所擾。

translations.literal: Ordered to attend the crown prince in visiting the Xiaoling tomb, on the road he restrained the troops so that not the slightest thing was disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to accompany the crown prince to the Xiaoling tomb, he kept the troops so disciplined that nothing was disturbed along the way.

sentences.zh: 太子欲獵，慶諫止。

translations.literal: The crown prince wished to hunt, and Qing remonstrated and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince wished to hunt, Qing dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 及太子還北京，遂留慶南京兵部。

translations.literal: When the crown prince returned to Beijing, Qing was left at the Nanjing Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince went back to Beijing, Qing remained at the Nanjing Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年，安遠侯柳升討黎利，命慶參贊軍務，許擇部曹賢能者自隨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande, the Marquis of Anyuan, Liu Sheng, campaigned against Le Loi; Qing was ordered to assist in military affairs and permitted to choose capable men from the ministries to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 2, Marquis Liu Sheng marched against Le Loi; Qing was ordered to advise on military affairs and allowed to take able ministry officers with him.

sentences.zh: 師至鎮夷關，升意輕賊，不為備。

translations.literal: When the army reached Zhenyi Pass, Sheng held the enemy lightly and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenyi Pass, Sheng underestimated the enemy and took no precautions.

sentences.zh: 郎中史安、主事陳鏞言於慶。

translations.literal: Director Shi An and Registrar Chen Yong spoke to Qing about it.
translations.idiomatic: Director Shi An and Registrar Chen Yong warned Qing.

sentences.zh: 時慶已病甚，強起告升。

translations.literal: At the time Qing was already gravely ill; he forced himself up to inform Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was already desperately ill but dragged himself up to warn Sheng.

sentences.zh: 升不聽，直前，中伏敗死。

translations.literal: Sheng would not listen, advanced straight ahead, fell into an ambush, and died in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng would not listen, pushed forward, was ambushed, and died.

sentences.zh: 慶病遂篤，明日亦死，一軍盡沒。

translations.literal: Qing's illness then became severe; the next day he also died, and the whole army was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Qing's illness worsened and he died the next day; the entire army was lost.

sentences.zh: 師逵，字九達，東阿人。

translations.literal: Shi Kui, styled Jiuda, was a native of Dong'e.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kui, styled Jiuda, came from Dong'e.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事母至孝。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he served his mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father young and served his mother with the utmost devotion.

sentences.zh: 年十三，母疾，思藤花菜。

translations.literal: At age thirteen, when his mother was ill, she longed for wisteria flowers and greens.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen, when his mother fell ill, she craved wisteria greens.

sentences.zh: 逵出城南二十餘里求得之。

translations.literal: Kui went more than twenty li south of the city and obtained them.
translations.idiomatic: Kui walked more than twenty li south of the city to find them.

sentences.zh: 及歸，夜二鼓，遇虎。

translations.literal: When he returned, it was the second watch of the night, and he met a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, near the second watch of night, he met a tiger.

sentences.zh: 逵驚呼天，虎舍之去。

translations.literal: Kui cried out to Heaven in alarm; the tiger released him and left.
translations.idiomatic: Kui cried out to Heaven; the tiger let him go.

sentences.zh: 母疾尋愈。

translations.literal: His mother's illness soon recovered.
translations.idiomatic: His mother soon recovered.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，以國子生從御史出按事，為御史所劾，逮至。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign, as a student of the Imperial Academy he followed a censor on an inspection tour and was impeached by the censor; he was arrested and brought in.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, as an Imperial Academy student on censorial duty he was impeached by the censor and arrested.

sentences.zh: 帝偉其貌，釋之，謫御史臺書案牘。

translations.literal: The emperor admired his appearance, released him, and demoted him to clerical work at the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his looks, freed him, and demoted him to clerical work at the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢御史，遷陜西按察使。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to censor and transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In time he became a censor, then Surveillance Commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 獄囚淹系千人，浹旬盡決遣，悉當其罪。

translations.literal: A thousand prisoners were long detained; within ten days he decided and dispatched them all, and every case matched its crime.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand prisoners languished in jail; within ten days he tried and released them all, and every sentence fit the crime.

sentences.zh: 母憂去官，廬墓側，不飲酒食肉者三年。

translations.literal: He left office for his mother's mourning and built a hut beside her tomb, eating no meat and drinking no wine for three years.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned for his mother's mourning, built a hut by her tomb, and ate no meat or wine for three years.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，召為兵部侍郎，改吏部。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, he was summoned as Vice Minister of War and then transferred to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On the Yongle Emperor's accession he was made Vice Minister of War, then transferred to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年建北京宮殿，分遣大臣出采木。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongle the Beijing palaces were built, and ministers were sent out separately to gather timber.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 4, as the Beijing palaces were built, senior ministers were sent to procure timber.

sentences.zh: 逵往湖、湘，以十萬眾入山辟道路，召商賈，軍役得貿易，事以辦。

translations.literal: Kui went to Hunan and Hubei; with a hundred thousand men he entered the mountains to open roads, summoned merchants, and soldiers and laborers were able to trade, so the task was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Kui went to Hunan and Hubei; with a hundred thousand men he cut mountain roads, drew in merchants, and let troops trade so the work was finished.

sentences.zh: 然頗嚴刻，民不堪，多從李法良為亂。

translations.literal: Yet he was rather harsh and exacting; the people could not bear it and many followed Li Faliang in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: But he was harsh; the people could not endure it and many joined Li Faliang's revolt.

sentences.zh: 左中允周幹劾之。

translations.literal: Left Palace Companion Zhou Gan impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Left Palace Companion Zhou Gan impeached him.

sentences.zh: 時仁宗監國，以帝所特遣，置不問。

translations.literal: At the time the crown prince was supervising the realm; because the emperor had specially dispatched Kui, the matter was set aside.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was then regent; because the emperor had personally sent Kui, the charge was ignored.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝北征，命總督饋餉，逵請量程置頓堡，更遞轉輸。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the emperor campaigned north, he was ordered to supervise provisions; Kui asked to set relay forts according to distance and rotate transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, on the northern campaign, he was put in charge of supplies; Kui proposed relay forts by distance and rotating transport.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 逵佐蹇義在吏部二十年，人不敢幹以私。

translations.literal: Kui assisted Jian Yi in the Ministry of Personnel for twenty years; no one dared approach him with private requests.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty years Kui assisted Jian Yi at Personnel; no one dared solicit him privately.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嗣位，與趙羾、古樸皆改官南京，而逵進戶部尚書，兼掌吏部。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor succeeded, he and Zhao Gong and Gu Pu were all transferred to Nanjing posts, while Kui was advanced to Minister of Revenue and also managed Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Renzong Emperor, he, Zhao Gong, and Gu Pu were moved to Nanjing posts, while Kui became Minister of Revenue and also oversaw Personnel.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年正月卒官，年六十二。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Xuande he died in office, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the first month of Xuande 2, aged sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 逵廉，不殖生產，祿賜皆分宗黨。

translations.literal: Kui was incorrupt and did not amass property; stipends and gifts he all divided among his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was honest and amassed nothing; he divided stipends and gifts among his kin.

sentences.zh: 有子八人，至無以自贍。

translations.literal: He had eight sons, yet in the end they could not support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons who could scarcely support themselves.

sentences.zh: 成祖在北京嘗語左右曰：「六部扈從臣，不貪者惟逵而已。」

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor once said to those around him in Beijing: 'Among the six ministries' attendant ministers, the only one who is not greedy is Kui alone.
translations.idiomatic: At Beijing the Yongle Emperor once told his attendants: 'Of the six ministries' ministers who follow me, only Kui is not greedy.

sentences.zh: 古樸，字文質，陳州人。

translations.literal: Gu Pu, styled Wenzhi, was a native of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Pu, styled Wenzhi, came from Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武中以太學生清理郡縣田賦圖籍，還隸五軍斷事理刑。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign, as an Imperial Academy student he sorted out prefectural and county land-tax registers and maps, then returned to serve in the Five Armies Office judging criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, as an academy student he sorted prefectural land-tax registers, then served in the Five Armies Office judging cases.

sentences.zh: 自陳家貧，願得祿養母。

translations.literal: He himself stated that his family was poor and he wished to receive a salary to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He said his family was poor and he wished for a salary to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，除工部主事。

translations.literal: The emperor commended this and appointed him Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and made him a director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 母歿，官給舟歸葬。

translations.literal: When his mother died, the government provided a boat for his return burial.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, the government gave him a boat for the funeral journey.

sentences.zh: 服闋，改兵部，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was transferred to War and successively promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he moved to War and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 建文三年擢兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianwen he was promoted to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwen 3 he became Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，改戶部。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, he was transferred to Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On the Yongle Emperor's accession he was moved to Revenue.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年，樸奏：「先奉詔令江西、湖廣及蘇、松諸府輸糧北京，今聞並患水潦，轉運艱難，而北京諸郡歲幸豐。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle, Pu memorialized: 'Earlier we received an edict ordering Jiangxi, Huguang, and the prefectures of Suzhou and Songjiang to deliver grain to Beijing. Now we hear that all suffer from flood, transport is difficult, while the districts around Beijing have had good harvests year after year.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 2, Pu memorialized: 'An earlier edict required Jiangxi, Huguang, and Suzhou-Songjiang to ship grain to Beijing. All now suffer floods and transport is hard, while the Beijing region has had good harvests.

sentences.zh: 宜發鈔命有司增價收糴，減南方運。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to issue paper money ordering the officials to buy grain at a higher price and reduce southern transport.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed issuing paper money for local officials to buy grain at a premium and cut southern shipments.'

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 營建北京，命采木江西，以恤民見褒。

translations.literal: In building Beijing he was ordered to gather timber in Jiangxi and was praised for showing compassion to the people.
translations.idiomatic: When timber was gathered in Jiangxi for Beijing, he was praised for sparing the people.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝北巡，皇太子監國。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the emperor toured north and the crown prince supervised the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the emperor toured the north while the crown prince governed.

sentences.zh: 召還，佐夏原吉理戶部。

translations.literal: Pu was recalled to assist Xia Yuanji in managing Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was recalled to help Xia Yuanji run Revenue.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，改南京通政使。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor took the throne, he was made Commissioner of the Nanjing Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Renzong Emperor he became Nanjing Commissioner of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 明年就拜戶部尚書，出督畿內田賦。

translations.literal: The next year he was immediately appointed Minister of Revenue and sent out to supervise land tax within the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made Minister of Revenue and sent to oversee capital-region land tax.

sentences.zh: 師逵病，命樸代之。

translations.literal: Shi Kui fell ill and Pu was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Kui fell ill, Pu replaced him.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年二月卒於官。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Xuande he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the second month of Xuande 3.

sentences.zh: 初，戶部主事劉良不檢，乞中貴人求上考。

translations.literal: Earlier, Revenue Director Liu Liang was unrestrained and begged a palace eunuch to seek a top evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Revenue Director Liu Liang was unscrupulous and asked a palace eunuch to secure a top rating.

sentences.zh: 樸不可。

translations.literal: Pu would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Pu refused.

sentences.zh: 良遂誣奏樸罪，樸就逮。

translations.literal: Liang then falsely memorialized accusing Pu of a crime, and Pu was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Liang then falsely accused Pu, who was arrested.

sentences.zh: 成祖察其誣，得釋。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor saw that it was a false charge and released him.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor saw the charge was false and freed him.

sentences.zh: 他日，吏部奏予良誥。

translations.literal: Another day, the Ministry of Personnel memorialized granting Liang an edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Later Personnel memorialized granting Liang a commendation edict.

sentences.zh: 仁宗曰：「此人素無行，且嘗誣大臣，不可與。」

translations.literal: The Renzong Emperor said: 'This man has always been without conduct, and moreover once falsely accused a great minister—it cannot be granted.'
translations.idiomatic: The Renzong Emperor said: 'This man has always been worthless and once slandered a senior minister; it cannot be granted.'

sentences.zh: 良後果以贓敗。

translations.literal: Liang afterward indeed fell through corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was later ruined by corruption.

sentences.zh: 樸在朝三十余年，自郎署至尚書，確然有守，不通幹請，與右都御史向寶，俱以清介稱。

translations.literal: Pu was at court more than thirty years; from bureau director to minister he was firmly principled and would not accept solicitations; together with Right Censor-in-chief Xiang Bao he was both known for pure integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Pu served over thirty years, from director to minister, steadfast and free of solicitations; with Right Censor-in-chief Xiang Bao he was famed for integrity.

sentences.zh: 寶，字克忠，進賢人。

translations.literal: Bao, styled Kezhong, was a native of Jinxian.
translations.idiomatic: Bao, styled Kezhong, came from Jinxian.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，以進士授兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign, as a presented scholar he was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, as a presented scholar he became War vice director.

sentences.zh: 九年無過，擢通政使，以不善奏對力辭，改應天府尹。

translations.literal: Nine years without fault, he was promoted to Commissioner of Transmission; because he was not skilled at court responses he firmly declined and was made prefect of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years without fault he was made Commissioner of Transmission; unskilled at court responses, he firmly declined and became prefect of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 建文時，坐事謫廣西。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign, for an offense he was demoted to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen, for an offense he was exiled to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，召復職。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, he was summoned and restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, he was recalled and restored.

sentences.zh: 已，復坐事下獄，降兩浙鹽運判官。

translations.literal: Later, again for an offense he was imprisoned and demoted to Salt Transport Judge of the Two Zhes.
translations.idiomatic: Later, again for an offense he was imprisoned and demoted to Salt Transport Judge of the Two Zhes.

sentences.zh: 仁宗在東宮，知其廉。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor was crown prince, he knew Bao's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong Emperor was crown prince, he knew Bao's integrity.

sentences.zh: 及即位，召為右都御史兼詹事，並給兩俸。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Bao was summoned as Right Censor-in-chief and concurrently Director of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent, with both stipends granted.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession he summoned Bao as Right Censor-in-chief and concurrent Director of the Heir Apparent's Household, with both stipends.

sentences.zh: 尋應詔陳八事，多可采者。

translations.literal: Soon, responding to an edict, he presented eight proposals, many of which were worth adopting.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, answering an edict, he presented eight proposals, many of them worth adopting.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，改南京。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuande he was transferred to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuande he was transferred to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 三年入覲，帝憫其老，命致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year he came to audience; the emperor pitied his age and ordered him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he came to audience; pitying his age, the emperor ordered him to retire.

sentences.zh: 歸，卒於途。

translations.literal: Returning home, he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: On the journey home he died on the road.

sentences.zh: 寶有文學，寬厚愛民，而持身廉直，屢遭困厄不稍易，平居言不及利。

translations.literal: Bao had literary learning, was generous and loved the people, yet maintained himself upright and incorrupt; repeatedly meeting hardship he did not change in the slightest, and in ordinary speech never touched on profit.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was learned, generous, and loved the people, yet remained upright; though often in distress he never wavered and never spoke of gain.

sentences.zh: 歷仕四十余年，卒之日，家具蕭然。

translations.literal: He served in office more than forty years; on the day he died his household furnishings were bare.
translations.idiomatic: He served more than forty years and died with bare furnishings at home.

sentences.zh: 陳壽，隨人。

translations.literal: Chen Shou was a native of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou came from Sui.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，由國子生授戶部主事。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign, from a student of the Imperial Academy he was appointed Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, from the Imperial Academy he became a Revenue director.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年遷員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle he was transferred to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1 he was made vice director.

sentences.zh: 出為山東參政，所至以愛民為務。

translations.literal: Sent out as Administration Vice Commissioner of Shandong, wherever he went he made loving the people his task.
translations.idiomatic: As Shandong Administration Vice Commissioner, wherever he went he put the people first.

sentences.zh: 用夏原吉薦，召為工部左侍郎。

translations.literal: On Xia Yuanji's recommendation he was summoned as Left Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On Xia Yuanji's recommendation he was summoned as Left Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 皇太子監國南京，壽日陳兵民困，又乘間言左右幹恩澤者多，恐累明德。

translations.literal: When the crown prince governed Nanjing, Shou daily reported the distress of soldiers and civilians and also seized occasions to say that many around the prince sought favors, fearing this would stain his bright virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince governed Nanjing, Shou daily reported military and civilian distress and also warned that many around the prince sought favors, fearing this would stain his virtue.

sentences.zh: 太子深納之。

translations.literal: The crown prince deeply accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince took this deeply to heart.

sentences.zh: 嘗目送之出，顧侍臣曰：「侍郎中第一人也。」

translations.literal: Once, watching him leave, he turned to his attendants and said: "Of all the vice ministers, he is the foremost."
translations.idiomatic: Once, watching him leave, he told his attendants: "Of all the vice ministers, he is the foremost."

sentences.zh: 九年以漢王高煦譖，下獄，貧不能給朝夕。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, on the slander of Prince Han Gaoxu, he was imprisoned; poor, he could not provide for day and night.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, slandered by Prince Han Gaoxu, he was imprisoned and was too poor to live.

sentences.zh: 官屬有饋之者，拒不受，竟死獄中。

translations.literal: When colleagues offered him gifts, he refused to accept and in the end died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: When colleagues offered gifts, he refused them and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 逾年，啟殯如生。

translations.literal: More than a year later, when the coffin was opened his body was as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, when the coffin was opened his body looked as if alive.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，贈工部尚書，謚敏肅，官其子常中書舍人，後亦至工部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor took the throne, Shou was posthumously made Minister of Works with the posthumous name Minsu; his son Chang was appointed Secretariat Drafter, and later also rose to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong Emperor succeeded, Shou was posthumously made Minister of Works with the name Minsu; his son Chang was made Secretariat Drafter and later also rose to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 與壽同下獄死者，有馬京、許思溫。

translations.literal: Those who died in prison together with Chen Shou were Ma Jing and Xu Siwen.
translations.idiomatic: Those who died in prison with Chen Shou were Ma Jing and Xu Siwen.

sentences.zh: 京，武功人。

translations.literal: Jing was a native of Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jing came from Wugong.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，以進士授翰林編修，歷左通政、大理卿。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign, as a presented scholar he was appointed Hanlin Academician Editor, and successively served as Left Vice Commissioner of Transmission and Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, as a presented scholar he became Hanlin Editor, then Left Vice Commissioner of Transmission and Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年為行部左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle he became Left Vice Minister of the traveling ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1 he was Left Vice Minister of the traveling ministry.

sentences.zh: 皇太子守北京，命兼輔導，盡誠翊贊，太子甚重之。

translations.literal: When the crown prince guarded Beijing, he was ordered also to instruct and assist; he devoted himself fully in support, and the crown prince greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince held Beijing, he was told to instruct and assist him and won the prince's deep trust.

sentences.zh: 數為高煦所譖，謫戍廣西，仍坐前事，逮下獄。

translations.literal: Several times he was slandered by Gaoxu, demoted to garrison Guangxi, and still implicated in the earlier affair was arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoxu slandered him repeatedly; he was demoted to Guangxi, then arrested again on the old charge.

sentences.zh: 思溫，字叔雍，吳人。

translations.literal: Siwen, styled Shuyong, was a native of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Siwen, styled Shuyong, came from Wu.

sentences.zh: 以國子生署刑部主事，累官北平按察副使。

translations.literal: As a student of the Imperial Academy he acted as Registrar of the Ministry of Punishments and rose to Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: As an academy student he served as acting Registrar of Punishments and rose to Beiping Vice Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 燕師起，思溫佐城守有勞，擢刑部侍郎，改吏部，兼贊善。

translations.literal: When the Yan army rose, Siwen assisted in defending the city with merit, was promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments, transferred to Personnel, and also served as Instructor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan forces rose, he helped defend the city, became Vice Minister of Punishments, then Personnel, and also Instructor.

sentences.zh: 亦以讒下獄。

translations.literal: He also was slandered and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He too was slandered and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 皆瘐死。

translations.literal: Both died of illness in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Both died of illness in prison.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，贈京少傅，謚文簡；

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor took the throne, Jing was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Tutor of the Palace with the posthumous name Wenjian;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Renzong Emperor, Jing was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Palace with the name Wenjian;

sentences.zh: 思溫吏部尚書，官其子俊贊禮郎，進學翰林。

translations.literal: Siwen was made Minister of Personnel, his son Jun was appointed Supporter of Rites, and advanced to study in the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: Siwen was made Minister of Personnel; his son Jun was made Supporter of Rites and entered the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 劉季篪，名韶，以字行，余姚人。

translations.literal: Liu Jichi, personal name Shao, known by his style, was a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jichi, personal name Shao, known by his style name, came from Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 洪武中進士。

translations.literal: Presented scholar in the Hongwu reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination under Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 除行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a courier.

sentences.zh: 使朝鮮，卻其饋贐。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to Korea, he declined their gifts.
translations.idiomatic: As envoy to Korea he refused their gifts.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，賜衣鈔，擢陜西參政。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he granted robes and paper money and promoted him to Administration Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it, gave him robes and paper money, and made him Shaanxi Administration Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 陜有逋賦，有司峻刑督，民不能輸。

translations.literal: Shaanxi had arrears in tax; the officials used harsh punishment to compel payment, and the people could not deliver.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi had tax arrears; officials used harsh punishment and the people could not pay.

sentences.zh: 季篪至，與其僚分行郡縣，悉縱械者，緩為期。

translations.literal: When Jichi arrived, he and his colleagues divided among the prefectures and counties, released all who were in shackles, and granted extended deadlines.
translations.idiomatic: Jichi and his staff toured the prefectures, freed those in shackles, and granted extensions.

sentences.zh: 民感其德，悉完納。

translations.literal: The people were moved by his virtue and all completed payment.
translations.idiomatic: The people were grateful and paid in full.

sentences.zh: 陜不產碙砂，而歲有課。

translations.literal: Shaanxi did not produce sal ammoniac, yet there was an annual levy.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi produced no sal ammoniac, yet paid an annual levy for it.

sentences.zh: 季篪言於朝，罷之。

translations.literal: Jichi spoke to the court and it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Jichi memorialized and the levy was abolished.

sentences.zh: 洪渠水溢，為治堰蓄泄，遂為永利。

translations.literal: When the Hong Canal overflowed, he built dikes to store and release water, and it became a lasting benefit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hong Canal flooded, he built dikes to store and release the water to lasting benefit.

sentences.zh: 建文中，召為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign he was summoned as Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen he was summoned as Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 民有為盜所引者，逮至，盜已死，乃召盜妻子使識之。

translations.literal: A man was implicated by a thief; when brought in, the thief was already dead, so Jichi summoned the thief's wife and children to identify him.
translations.idiomatic: A man was implicated by a thief; when brought in the thief was dead, so Jichi had the thief's family identify him.

sentences.zh: 聽其辭，誣也，釋之。

translations.literal: Listening to their words, it was a false accusation, and he released the man.
translations.idiomatic: Their testimony showed a false charge, and he released the man.

sentences.zh: 吏虧官錢，誣千余人，悉為辨免。

translations.literal: A clerk was short in official funds and falsely implicated more than a thousand people; Jichi cleared them all.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk owed official funds and falsely implicated over a thousand people; Jichi cleared them all.

sentences.zh: 河陽逆旅朱、趙二人異室寢。

translations.literal: At an inn in Heyang, two men surnamed Zhu and Zhao slept in separate rooms.
translations.idiomatic: At an inn in Heyang, Zhu and Zhao slept in separate rooms.

sentences.zh: 趙被殺，有司疑朱殺之，考掠誣服。

translations.literal: Zhao was murdered; the officials suspected Zhu had killed him and under torture he confessed falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was killed; officials suspected Zhu and tortured him into a false confession.

sentences.zh: 季篪獨曰：「是非夙仇，且其裝無可利。」

translations.literal: Jichi alone said: 'These were not old enemies, and moreover his belongings offered nothing to gain.'
translations.idiomatic: Jichi alone said: 'They were not old enemies, and his luggage held nothing worth killing for.'

sentences.zh: 緩其獄，竟得殺趙者。

translations.literal: He slowed the case, and in the end the man who killed Zhao was found.
translations.idiomatic: He delayed the trial and eventually found Zhao's real killer.

sentences.zh: 揚州民家，盜夜入殺人，遺刀屍傍，刀有記識，其鄰家也。

translations.literal: In a Yangzhou household a thief entered by night and killed someone, leaving a knife by the corpse; the knife bore a mark identifying a neighbor.
translations.idiomatic: In Yangzhou a thief killed someone at night and left a marked knife by the body that pointed to a neighbor.

sentences.zh: 官捕鞫之。

translations.literal: The officials arrested and interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: Officials arrested and interrogated the neighbor.

sentences.zh: 鄰曰：「失此刀久矣。」

translations.literal: The neighbor said: 'I lost this knife long ago.'
translations.idiomatic: The neighbor said: 'I lost that knife long ago.'

sentences.zh: 不勝掠，誣服。

translations.literal: Unable to bear the beating, he confessed falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Under torture he falsely confessed.

sentences.zh: 季篪使人懷刀就其裏潛察之。

translations.literal: Jichi had a man carry the knife and secretly examine the neighbor's household.
translations.idiomatic: Jichi sent someone with the knife to search the neighbor's house in secret.

sentences.zh: 一童子識曰：「此吾家物。」

translations.literal: A child recognized it and said: 'This is from our house.'
translations.idiomatic: A child recognized it and said: 'That is ours.'

sentences.zh: 盜乃得。

translations.literal: The thief was thereby obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The real thief was caught.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，纂修《大典》，命姚廣孝、解縉及季篪總其事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, in compiling the Great Compendium, Yao Guangxiao, Xie Jin, and Jichi were ordered to oversee the task.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle, Yao Guangxiao, Xie Jin, and Jichi were put in charge of compiling the Great Compendium.

sentences.zh: 八年坐失出下獄，謫外任。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was imprisoned for a lapse in release, and demoted to an outside post.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was jailed for an error in releasing prisoners and demoted to an outside post.

sentences.zh: 逡巡未行，復下獄。

translations.literal: Hesitating and not yet departing, he was again imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave he was imprisoned again.

sentences.zh: 久之始釋。

translations.literal: After a long time he was finally released.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long interval was he freed.

sentences.zh: 命以儒服隸翰林院編纂。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve the Hanlin Academy in compilation wearing scholar's dress.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to compile at the Hanlin in scholar's dress.

sentences.zh: 尋授工部主事，卒於官。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Director in the Ministry of Works and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a Works director and died in office.

sentences.zh: 劉辰，字伯靜，金華人。

translations.literal: Liu Chen, styled Bojing, was a native of Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chen, styled Bojing, came from Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 國初，以署典簽使方國珍。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty, he served as acting Document Attendant to Fang Guozhen.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding he served as acting Document Attendant to Fang Guozhen.

sentences.zh: 國珍飾二姬以進，叱卻之。

translations.literal: Guozhen adorned two concubines to present to him; he rebuked and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen offered him two adorned concubines; he refused them.

sentences.zh: 李文忠駐師嚴州，辟置幕下。

translations.literal: Li Wenzhong stationed troops at Yanzhou and recruited him to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenzhong camped at Yanzhou and took him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 元帥葛俊守廣信，盛冬發民浚城濠。

translations.literal: Marshal Ge Jun held Guangxin; in deep winter he conscripted the people to dredge the moat.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Ge Jun held Guangxin and in deep winter conscripted the people to dredge the moat.

sentences.zh: 文忠止之。

translations.literal: Wenzhong stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong forbade it.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: Jun would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Jun would not listen.

sentences.zh: 文忠怒，欲臨以兵。

translations.literal: Wenzhong was angry and wished to advance troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong grew angry and meant to march against him.

sentences.zh: 辰請往諭之。

translations.literal: Chen asked to go and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen asked to go and reason with him.

sentences.zh: 俊悔謝，事遂已。

translations.literal: Jun repented and apologized, and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Jun repented and the matter ended.

sentences.zh: 以親老辭歸。

translations.literal: He cited aged parents and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded aged parents and went home.

sentences.zh: 建文中，用薦擢監察御史，出知鎮江府，勤於職事。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign, on recommendation he was promoted to Investigating Censor and sent out as prefect of Zhenjiang, diligent in his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen, recommended, he became Investigating Censor and then prefect of Zhenjiang, where he was diligent.

sentences.zh: 瀕江田八十余頃，久淪於水，賦如故，以辰言得除。

translations.literal: More than eighty qing of riverside fields along the river had long been submerged, yet the tax remained as before; on Chen's word it was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Over eighty qing of riverside land had lain under water while tax was still levied; Chen had the levy removed.

sentences.zh: 京口閘廢，轉漕者道新河出江，舟數敗。

translations.literal: The Jingkou sluice had fallen into disuse; those turning transport went out to the river by the new canal, and boats were often wrecked.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingkou sluice was abandoned; transport used the new canal to reach the river and boats were often wrecked.

sentences.zh: 辰修故閘，公私皆便。

translations.literal: Chen restored the old sluice, to the convenience of both public and private interests.
translations.idiomatic: Chen restored the old sluice, to everyone's benefit.

sentences.zh: 漕河易涸，仰練湖益水，三鬥門久廢。

translations.literal: The transport canal easily dried up; the Lian Lake supplemented its water, but the three sluice gates had long been abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The canal often ran dry; water from Lian Lake helped, but three sluice gates had long been ruined.

sentences.zh: 辰修築之，運舟既通，湖下田益稔。

translations.literal: Chen repaired them; transport boats could pass, and the fields below the lake grew richer.
translations.idiomatic: Chen rebuilt them; transport flowed again and fields below the lake prospered.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，李景隆言辰知國初事，召至，預修《太祖實錄》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, Li Jinglong said Chen knew affairs of the founding era and he was summoned to take part in compiling the Veritable Records of the Taizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle, Li Jinglong said Chen knew founding-era affairs; he was summoned to help compile the Taizu Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 遷江西布政司參政，奏蠲九郡荒田糧。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administration Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi and memorialized remitting grain tax on wasteland in nine prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He became Jiangxi Administration Vice Commissioner and memorialized remitting tax on wasteland in nine prefectures.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，勸富民貸饑者，蠲其徭役以為之息。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he urged the wealthy to lend to the hungry and remitted their corvée labor as interest.
translations.idiomatic: In famine he urged the rich to lend to the hungry and remitted their labor service as interest.

sentences.zh: 官為立券，期年而償。

translations.literal: The government established bonds, to be repaid within a year.
translations.idiomatic: The government issued bonds repayable within a year.

sentences.zh: 辰居官廉勤尚氣，與都司、按察使不相得，數爭，坐免官。

translations.literal: Chen in office was incorrupt, diligent, and spirited; he did not get along with the regional military commission and surveillance commission, quarreled repeatedly, and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was honest, diligent, and proud; he clashed with the regional military and surveillance commissions, quarreled often, and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 十四年起行部左侍郎，復留南京者三年。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was raised to Left Vice Minister of the traveling ministry and again remained at Nanjing for three years.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became Left Vice Minister of the traveling ministry and stayed at Nanjing three more years.

sentences.zh: 帝念其老，賜敕及鈔幣，今致仕。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful of his age, granted an edict and paper money and ordered him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of his age, the emperor gave him an edict, paper money, and retirement.

sentences.zh: 卒於途，年七十八。

translations.literal: He died on the road, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the journey home, aged seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 楊砥，字大用，澤州人。

translations.literal: Yang Di, styled Dayong, was a native of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Di, styled Dayong, came from Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武末，由進士授行人司右司副。

translations.literal: At the end of the Hongwu reign, as a presented scholar he was appointed Right Assistant Director of the Courier Office.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Hongwu, as a presented scholar he became Right Assistant Director of the Courier Office.

sentences.zh: 上疏言：「揚雄為莽大夫，貽譏萬世。

translations.literal: He memorialized saying: 'Yang Xiong served as Grand Master to Wang Mang and earned ridicule for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: 'Yang Xiong served Wang Mang as Grand Master and has been mocked for ages.

sentences.zh: 董仲舒《天人三策》及正誼明道之言，足以扶翼世教。

translations.literal: Dong Zhongshu's 'Three Strategies of Heaven and Man' and his words on righteous principle and the Way were enough to support the teachings of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu's Three Strategies and his doctrine of righteous principle could uphold the age's teaching.

sentences.zh: 今孔廟從祀有雄無仲舒，非是。」

translations.literal: Now in the Confucian temple accompanying sacrifice there is Xiong but not Zhongshu—this is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Confucian temple honors Xiong but not Zhongshu—that is wrong.'

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 歷官湖廣布政司參議。

translations.literal: He served in office as Administration Vice Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Huguang Administration Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 建文中，言：「帝堯之德始於親九族。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign he said: 'The virtue of Emperor Yao began in cherishing the nine branches of kin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen he said: 'Emperor Yao's virtue began in cherishing his kin.

sentences.zh: 今宜惇睦諸藩，無自剪枝葉。」

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to show cordial harmony to all the feudatories and not prune one's own branches and leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Now the feudal princes should be treated with cordial harmony, not pruned like branches.'

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: There was no response.

sentences.zh: 父喪歸。

translations.literal: He returned home for his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He went home for his father's mourning.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，起鴻臚寺卿，乞終制。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, Di was summoned to Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and begged to complete mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, Di was summoned as Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and begged to complete mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，擢禮部侍郎，坐視河渠失職，降工部主事，改禮部。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites; for neglecting his duty over canals he was demoted to Works director, then transferred back to Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was made Vice Minister of Rites; for neglecting the canals he was demoted to a Works director, then moved back to Rites.

sentences.zh: 永樂十年遷北京行太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongle he was transferred to Chief Minister of the traveling Court of the Imperial Stud in Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 10 he became Chief Minister of the traveling Court of the Imperial Stud in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 時吳橋至天津大水決堤傷稼。

translations.literal: At the time from Wuqiao to Tianjin great floods breached the dikes and damaged the crops.
translations.idiomatic: At the time great floods from Wuqiao to Tianjin breached the dikes and ruined the harvest.

sentences.zh: 砥請開德州東南黃河故道及土河，以殺水勢。

translations.literal: Di asked to reopen the old Yellow River course southeast of Dezhou and the earthen canal to reduce the water's force.
translations.idiomatic: Di asked to reopen the old Yellow River course southeast of Dezhou and the earthen canal to reduce the flood.

sentences.zh: 帝命工部侍郎藺芳經理之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Vice Minister of Works Lan Fang to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Vice Minister of Works Lan Fang to oversee the work.

sentences.zh: 定牧馬法，請令民五丁養種馬一匹，十馬立群頭一人，五十馬立群長一人，養馬家歲蠲租糧之半。

translations.literal: He established horse-breeding law, asking that every five households raise one stud horse, one herd head per ten horses, one herd leader per fifty, and horse-raising households be granted half remission of grain tax each year.
translations.idiomatic: He set horse-breeding rules: every five households would raise one stud horse, one herd head per ten horses, one herd leader per fifty, and horse-raising households would receive half remission of grain tax each year.

sentences.zh: 而薊州以東至山海諸衛，土地寬廣，水草豐美，其屯軍人養種馬一匹，租亦免半。

translations.literal: From Jizhou east to the guards at Shanhai the land was broad and grass and water abundant; each garrison soldier would raise one stud horse and also receive half rent remission.
translations.idiomatic: From Jizhou east to the Shanhai guards the land was broad and well watered; each garrison soldier would raise one stud horse and also receive half rent remission.

sentences.zh: 帝命軍租盡蠲之，余悉從其議。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered full rent remission for the soldiers and followed the rest of his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered full rent remission for the soldiers and accepted the rest of his proposals.

sentences.zh: 於是馬大蕃息。

translations.literal: Horses then flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Horses then multiplied greatly.

sentences.zh: 砥剛介有守，尤篤孝行。

translations.literal: Di was upright and principled, and especially devoted in filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Di was upright and principled, especially filial.

sentences.zh: 十六年，母喪哀毀，未至家，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, in mourning for his mother he grieved to destruction; before reaching home he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, mourning his mother, he grieved himself to death on the road home.

sentences.zh: 虞謙，字伯益，金壇人。

translations.literal: Yu Qian, styled Boyi, was a native of Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian, styled Boyi, came from Jintan.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，由國子生擢刑部郎中，出知杭州府。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign, from a student of the Imperial Academy he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Punishments and sent out as prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, from the Imperial Academy he became Punishments director, then prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 建文中請限僧道田，人無過十畝，余以均給貧民。
