translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign he asked to limit monastic and Daoist land to ten mu per person, the remainder to be equally distributed to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen he proposed limiting monastic and Daoist land to ten mu per person and distributing the rest to the poor.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 永樂初召為大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 時有詔。

translations.literal: At the time there was an edict.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued.

sentences.zh: 建文中，上言改舊制者悉面陳。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign, all who had memorialized changing old institutions were to state them in person.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen, anyone who had changed old institutions was to report in person.

sentences.zh: 謙乃言前事請罪。

translations.literal: Qian then spoke of his former matter and asked for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Qian then confessed his earlier proposal and asked to be punished.

sentences.zh: 帝見謙怖，笑曰：「此秀才辟老、佛耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor, seeing Qian afraid, laughed and said: 'This scholar is merely driving off Laozi and the Buddha.'
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Qian frightened, the emperor laughed: 'This scholar only wanted to drive out Laozi and Buddha.'

sentences.zh: 釋弗問。

translations.literal: He released him and did not inquire further.
translations.idiomatic: He released him without further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 而僧道限田制竟罷。

translations.literal: Yet the system limiting monastic and Daoist land was in the end abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The monastic land limit was nevertheless abolished.

sentences.zh: 都察院論誆騙罪，準洪武榜例梟首以徇。

translations.literal: The Censorate judged the crime of fraud according to the Hongwu posted example of decapitation and public display.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate sentenced fraud under the Hongwu posted example of decapitation.

sentences.zh: 謙奏：「比奉詔準律斷罪，誆騙當杖流，梟首非詔書意。」

translations.literal: Qian memorialized: 'We have lately received an edict to judge crimes according to the code; fraud should receive beating and exile—decapitation is not the edict's intent.'
translations.idiomatic: Qian memorialized: 'The new edict requires judging by the code; fraud warrants beating and exile, not decapitation.'

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 天津衛倉災，焚糧數十萬石。

translations.literal: At the Tianjin garrison granary there was a disaster and several hundred thousand piculs of grain were burned.
translations.idiomatic: Fire at the Tianjin garrison granary destroyed hundreds of thousands of piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 御史言主者盜用多，縱火自蓋。

translations.literal: Censors said the chief had stolen much and set fire to cover it.
translations.idiomatic: Censors said the chief had embezzled heavily and set the fire to cover it.

sentences.zh: 逮幾八百人，應死者百。

translations.literal: Nearly eight hundred were arrested, and a hundred were liable to death.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly eight hundred were arrested and a hundred faced death.

sentences.zh: 謙白其濫，得論減。

translations.literal: Qian showed the excess of the case and secured reduced sentences.
translations.idiomatic: Qian showed the case was excessive and secured lighter sentences.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝北巡，皇太子奏謙為右副都御史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the emperor toured north, the crown prince memorialized Qian as Right Vice Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, while the emperor toured north, the crown prince made Qian Right Vice Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 明年，偕給事中杜欽巡視淮、鳳抵陳州災傷，免田租，贖民所鬻子女。

translations.literal: The next year, together with Secretariat Receiver Du Qin, he inspected Huai and Feng to Chenzhou disaster areas, remitted land tax, and redeemed children the people had sold.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, with Du Qin, he inspected disaster areas from Huai-Feng to Chenzhou, remitted land tax, and redeemed children the people had sold.

sentences.zh: 明年，謙請振，太子諭之曰：「軍民困極，而卿等從容請啟，彼汲黯何如人也。」

translations.literal: The next year Qian requested relief; the crown prince instructed him: 'Soldiers and civilians are in extreme distress, yet you gentlemen ask at leisure to open the matter—how does that compare to Ji An?'
translations.idiomatic: When Qian asked to open relief, the crown prince said: 'People are starving and you ask at leisure—what would Ji An think?'

sentences.zh: 尋命督兩浙、蘇、松諸府糧，輸南、北京及徐州、淮安。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to supervise grain in Zhejiang, Suzhou, and Songjiang, delivering to Nanjing, Beijing, and Xuzhou and Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to supervise grain in Zhejiang, Suzhou, and Songjiang for delivery to Nanjing, Beijing, Xuzhou, and Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 富民賂有司，率得近地，而貧民多遠運。

translations.literal: The wealthy bribed officials and usually got nearby land, while the poor mostly transported over long distances.
translations.idiomatic: The rich bribed officials for nearby routes; the poor hauled grain long distances.

sentences.zh: 謙建議分四等：丁多糧最少者運北京，次少者運徐州，丁糧等者運南京、淮安，丁少糧多者存留本土。

translations.literal: Qian proposed dividing into four grades: those with many laborers and least grain should transport to Beijing; the next least to Xuzhou; equal labor and grain to Nanjing and Huai'an; few laborers and much grain to remain in their home region.
translations.idiomatic: Qian proposed four grades: most laborers and least grain to Beijing; next to Xuzhou; equal labor and grain to Nanjing and Huai'an; least labor and most grain to stay home.

sentences.zh: 民利賴之。

translations.literal: The people relied on this with benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The people benefited greatly.

sentences.zh: 又言：徐州、呂梁二洪，行舟多阻。

translations.literal: He also said: the Xuzhou and Lüliang rapids both hindered shipping.
translations.idiomatic: He also said the Xuzhou and Lüliang rapids blocked shipping.

sentences.zh: 請每洪增挽夫二百，月給廩；

translations.literal: He asked that at each rapid two hundred haulers be added, with monthly grain allowance;
translations.idiomatic: He asked for two hundred haulers at each rapid with monthly rations;

sentences.zh: 官牛一百，暇時聽民耕，大舟至，用以挽。

translations.literal: and a hundred government oxen, allowed to be farmed by the people in idle time; when large boats arrived they would be used to haul.
translations.idiomatic: and a hundred government oxen for peasants to farm in slack season and haul large boats when they arrived.

sentences.zh: 人以為便。

translations.literal: People regarded this as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: People found this convenient.

sentences.zh: 嘗督運木，役者大疫。

translations.literal: Once he supervised transport of timber and the laborers suffered a great epidemic.
translations.idiomatic: Once, supervising timber transport, laborers suffered a great epidemic.

sentences.zh: 謙令散處之，疫遂息。

translations.literal: Qian ordered them dispersed to quarters and the epidemic then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Qian had them dispersed to lodging and the epidemic ceased.

sentences.zh: 未幾，偕給事中許能巡撫浙江。

translations.literal: Before long, together with Secretariat Receiver Xu Neng, he toured and pacified Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, with Xu Neng, he toured and pacified Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，召還，改大理寺卿。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor took the throne, he was recalled and made Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Renzong Emperor he was recalled and made Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 時呂升為少卿，仰瞻為丞，而謙又薦嚴本為寺正。

translations.literal: At the time Lü Sheng was vice minister, Yang Zhan was assistant minister, and Qian also recommended Yan Ben as director of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Sheng was vice minister, Yang Zhan assistant minister, and Qian recommended Yan Ben as court director.

sentences.zh: 帝方矜慎刑獄，謙等亦悉心奏當。

translations.literal: The emperor was then cautious in punishments, and Qian and the others also devoted themselves to presenting fitting judgments.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was cautious with punishments; Qian and the others judged with care.

sentences.zh: 凡法司及四方所上獄，謙等再四參復，必求其平。

translations.literal: Whatever cases the judicial offices and the four directions submitted, Qian and the others reviewed repeatedly and always sought fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Every case from the judicial offices and the provinces they reviewed again and again for fairness.

sentences.zh: 嘗語人曰：「彼無憾，斯我無憾矣。」

translations.literal: He once said to people: 'If they have no regret, then I have no regret.'
translations.idiomatic: He once said: 'If they have no grievance, I have no grievance.'

sentences.zh: 嘗應詔上言七事，皆切中時務。

translations.literal: Once he responded to an edict with seven proposals, all hitting the needs of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Once he answered an edict with seven proposals, all timely.

sentences.zh: 有言其奏事不密，市恩於外者。

translations.literal: Someone said he did not keep his memorials secret and curried favor outside.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said he leaked memorials and curried favor abroad.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，降少卿。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and demoted him to vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and demoted him to vice minister.

sentences.zh: 一日，楊士奇奏事畢，不退。

translations.literal: One day, after Yang Shiqi had finished presenting affairs, he did not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: One day Yang Shiqi finished his business but did not leave.

sentences.zh: 帝問：「欲何言，得非為虞謙乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: 'What do you wish to say—is it not about Yu Qian?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: 'What more do you want to say—is it Yu Qian?'

sentences.zh: 士奇因具白其誣，且言謙歷事三朝，得大臣體。

translations.literal: Shiqi thereupon fully explained the false charge, and also said Qian had served three reigns and possessed the bearing of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi explained the slander and said Qian had served three reigns with a great minister's bearing.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾亦悔之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'I also regret it.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'I regret it too.'

sentences.zh: 遂命復職。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered Qian restored to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Qian restored to office.

sentences.zh: 宣宗立，謙言：「舊制，犯死罪者，罰役終身。

translations.literal: When the Xuande Emperor took the throne, Qian said: 'Under the old system, those guilty of capital crimes were punished with labor for life.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xuande Emperor, Qian said: 'Under the old system, capital offenders served labor for life.

sentences.zh: 今所犯不等，宜依輕重分年限。」

translations.literal: Now the offenses are not equal; it is fitting to set terms of years according to severity.
translations.idiomatic: Offenses differ now; terms should vary with severity.'

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Reply: approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年三月卒於官。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Xuande he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the third month of Xuande 2.

sentences.zh: 謙美儀觀，風采凝重。

translations.literal: Qian had a handsome appearance and a grave bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was handsome and grave in manner.

sentences.zh: 工詩畫，自負才望。

translations.literal: He was skilled in poetry and painting and prided himself on talent and reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote poetry and painted, and prided himself on his gifts.

sentences.zh: 工部侍郎蘇瓚以鄙猥班謙上，恒怏怏，人以是隘其量雲。

translations.literal: Works Vice Minister Su Zan ranked above Qian though base and vulgar; Qian was always displeased, and for this people considered his breadth of mind narrow.
translations.idiomatic: Works Vice Minister Su Zan, though coarse, ranked above him; Qian was always resentful, and people said his spirit was small.

sentences.zh: 呂升，山陰人。

translations.literal: Lü Sheng was a native of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Sheng came from Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 永樂初為溧陽教諭，歷官江西、福建按察僉事，所至有清慎聲。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle he was instructor at Liyang; in office as Surveillance Vice Commissioner in Jiangxi and Fujian, wherever he went he had a reputation for purity and caution.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle he taught at Liyang, then served as Surveillance Vice Commissioner in Jiangxi and Fujian, famed everywhere for integrity.

sentences.zh: 入為大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 宣德八年致仕卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xuande he retired and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired in Xuande 8 and died.

sentences.zh: 仰瞻，長洲人。

translations.literal: Yang Zhan was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhan came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 永樂中由虎賁衛經歷遷大理寺丞。

translations.literal: During Yongle, from Tiger Guard Regiment experience he was transferred to Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle he rose from the Tiger Guard Regiment to Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 正統間，宦官王振用事，百官多奔走其門，惟瞻與大理卿薛瑄不往。

translations.literal: During the Zhengtong reign, when the eunuch Wang Zhen held power, many officials hurried to his gate, but only Zhan and Chief Minister Xue Xuan did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengtong era, when Wang Zhen held power, officials flocked to his door, but only Zhan and Chief Minister Xue Xuan stayed away.

sentences.zh: 會與瑄辨殺夫冤獄，益忤振，下獄，謫戍大同。

translations.literal: Once, in arguing with Xuan a wrongful case of a wife who killed her husband, he further offended Zhen and was imprisoned and demoted to garrison Datong.
translations.idiomatic: When he and Xuan overturned a wrongful wife-murder case, he further offended Zhen, was jailed, and sent to garrison Datong.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，召為右寺丞，執法愈堅，在位者多不悅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingtai reign he was summoned as Right Assistant Minister; he enforced the law ever more firmly, and many in office were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingtai he was recalled as Right Assistant Minister and grew stricter in law, displeasing many colleagues.

sentences.zh: 移疾歸，加大理少卿。

translations.literal: He cited illness and returned home, and was given the added title of Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and went home, with the added title of Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 嚴本，字誌道，江陰人。

translations.literal: Yan Ben, styled Zhidao, was a native of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ben, styled Zhidao, came from Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 少通群籍，習法律，以傅霖《刑統賦》辭約義博，註者非一，乃著《輯義》四卷。

translations.literal: In youth he mastered many books and studied law; because Fu Lin's 'Rhymed Compendium of the Penal Code' was concise in wording and broad in meaning, though many had annotated it, he composed 'Collected Explanations' in four juan.
translations.idiomatic: Youthfully learned in many books and law, he found Fu Lin's Rhymed Compendium of the Penal Code concise yet broad; though many had annotated it, he wrote Collected Explanations in four juan.

sentences.zh: 永樂十一年以薦征，試以疑律，敷析明暢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongle he was summoned on recommendation; tested with doubtful statutes, his analysis was clear and fluent.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 11 he was summoned on recommendation and, tested on doubtful statutes, analyzed them clearly.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Punishments director.

sentences.zh: 侍郎張本掌部事，官吏少當意者，獨重本，疑獄輒俾訊之。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Zhang Ben managed the ministry; few officials pleased him, but he alone valued Ben, and doubtful cases were always entrusted to him for inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Zhang Ben ran the ministry; few officials pleased him, but he valued Ben alone and sent him doubtful cases.

sentences.zh: 奉命使徽州，時督辦後期，例罰工，本不忍迫民。

translations.literal: Ordered on mission to Huizhou, when supervision work was overdue the rule was labor punishment; Ben could not bear to press the people.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Huizhou, when supervision ran late the rule was labor service; Ben would not press the people.

sentences.zh: 或以為言，本曰：「吾辦矣。」

translations.literal: Some spoke of this; Ben said: 'I shall handle it.'
translations.idiomatic: When criticized, Ben said: 'I will handle it.'

sentences.zh: 蓋已寓書其子，鬻田為工作償也。

translations.literal: For he had already sent word to his son to sell fields to pay for the labor service.
translations.idiomatic: He had already written his son to sell fields to pay the labor fine.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，以刑部尚書金純及虞謙薦，改大理寺正。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor took the throne, on the recommendation of Punishments Minister Jin Chun and Yu Qian, he was made Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Renzong Emperor, on Jin Chun's and Yu Qian's recommendation, he became Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 斷獄者多以「知情故縱」及「大不敬」論罪。

translations.literal: Those judging cases often used 'knowing and deliberately conniving' and 'great irreverence' to convict.
translations.idiomatic: Judges often convicted on 'knowing connivance' and 'great irreverence.'

sentences.zh: 本爭之曰：「律自叛逆數條外，無『故縱』之文。

translations.literal: Ben contended: 'Apart from the several articles on rebellion, the code has no text on deliberate connivance.
translations.idiomatic: Ben argued: 'Apart from rebellion, the code has no deliberate connivance.

sentences.zh: 即『不敬』，情有重輕，豈可概入重比？」

translations.literal: Even for irreverence, circumstances have heavy and light degrees—how can one lump them all into the heavy comparison?'
translations.idiomatic: Even irreverence has degrees—how can all be lumped into the heaviest penalty?'

sentences.zh: 謙韙之，悉為駁正。

translations.literal: Qian approved this and all were rejected and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Qian agreed and all were overturned.

sentences.zh: 良鄉民失馬，疑其鄰，告於丞，拷死。

translations.literal: A man in Liangxiang lost a horse and suspected his neighbor; he reported to the assistant prefect, who tortured him to death.
translations.idiomatic: In Liangxiang a man lost a horse, suspected his neighbor, and reported to the assistant prefect, who tortured the neighbor to death.

sentences.zh: 丞坐決罰不如法，當徒，而告者坐絞。

translations.literal: The assistant prefect was sentenced for deciding punishment not according to law and should serve corvée; yet the accuser was sentenced to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant prefect was sentenced to corvée for improper sentencing, but the accuser to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 本曰：「丞罪當。

translations.literal: Ben said: 'The assistant prefect's crime stands.
translations.idiomatic: Ben said: 'The assistant prefect is rightly punished.

sentences.zh: 告者因疑而訴，律以誣告致死，是丞與告者各殺一人，可乎？」

translations.literal: The accuser sued on suspicion; by the code, false accusation causing death—does this mean the assistant prefect and the accuser each killed one person? Is that permissible?'
translations.idiomatic: The accuser sued on suspicion; under the code false accusation causing death—did assistant prefect and accuser each kill a man? How can that be?'

sentences.zh: 駁正之。

translations.literal: It was rejected and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The sentence was overturned.

sentences.zh: 莒縣屯卒奪民田，民訟於官，卒被笞。

translations.literal: Garrison soldiers in Juxian seized commoners' fields; the people sued in court and the soldiers were beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Juxian garrison soldiers seized civilians' land; the people sued and the soldiers were beaten.

sentences.zh: 夜盜民驢，民搜得之。

translations.literal: At night a soldier stole a commoner's donkey and the commoner searched and found him.
translations.idiomatic: At night a soldier stole a donkey; the owner caught him.

sentences.zh: 卒反以為誣，擒送千戶，民被禁死。

translations.literal: The soldier in turn said he had been slandered and seized the man and sent him to the company commander; the commoner died under detention.
translations.idiomatic: The soldier claimed slander, seized the owner, and sent him to the company commander; the owner died in custody.

sentences.zh: 法司坐千戶徒。

translations.literal: The judicial offices sentenced the company commander to corvée.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices sentenced the commander to corvée.

sentences.zh: 本曰：「千戶生，則死者冤矣。」

translations.literal: Ben said: 'If the company commander lives, then the dead man is wronged.'
translations.idiomatic: Ben said: 'If the commander lives, the dead man is wronged.'

sentences.zh: 遂正其故勘罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon the crime of deliberate false incrimination was applied correctly.
translations.idiomatic: The commander's crime of deliberate false incrimination was applied.

sentences.zh: 蘇州衛卒十余人夜劫客舟於河西務，一卒死。

translations.literal: More than ten soldiers of the Suzhou garrison at night robbed a passenger boat at Hexi Station; one soldier died.
translations.idiomatic: Over ten Suzhou garrison soldiers robbed a passenger boat at Hexi Station by night; one soldier died.

sentences.zh: 懼事覺，誣鄰舟解囚人為盜，其侶往救見殺。

translations.literal: Fearing the affair would be discovered, they falsely accused men on a neighboring boat who were escorting prisoners of being robbers; when their companions went to rescue them they were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing discovery, they accused escorts on a neighboring boat of robbery; when companions came to rescue, they were killed.

sentences.zh: 皆誣服。

translations.literal: All confessed falsely under torture.
translations.idiomatic: All confessed under torture.

sentences.zh: 本疑之曰：「解人與囚同舟。

translations.literal: Ben doubted and said: 'The escorts and prisoners were on the same boat.
translations.idiomatic: Ben doubted: 'Escorts and prisoners shared a boat.

sentences.zh: 為盜，囚必知之。」

translations.literal: If they were robbers, the prisoners must have known.'
translations.idiomatic: If they were robbers, the prisoners would have known.'

sentences.zh: 按驗，果得實，遂抵卒罪。

translations.literal: On investigation the facts were obtained, and the soldiers' crime was applied.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation proved the truth and the soldiers were punished.

sentences.zh: 本立身方嚴，非禮弗履。

translations.literal: Ben in conduct was upright and strict and would not tread on what was not ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Ben was upright and strict and would not step outside ritual.

sentences.zh: 其使徽也，知府饋酒肴亦不受。

translations.literal: When he was envoy to Huizhou, the prefect offered wine and food and he also would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: As envoy to Huizhou he would not accept even wine and food from the prefect.

sentences.zh: 年七十八卒。

translations.literal: He died aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 湯宗，字正傳，浙江平陽人。

translations.literal: Tang Zong, styled Zhengchuan, was a native of Pingyang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zong, styled Zhengchuan, came from Pingyang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 洪武末，由太學生擢河南按察僉事，改北平。

translations.literal: At the end of the Hongwu reign, from a student of the Imperial Academy he was promoted to Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Henan and transferred to Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Hongwu, from the Imperial Academy he became Henan Surveillance Vice Commissioner, then moved to Beiping.

sentences.zh: 建文時上變，言按察使陳瑛受燕邸金錢，有異謀。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign he reported a sudden change, saying Surveillance Commissioner Chen Ying had received gold from the Yan mansion and harbored a divergent plot.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen he reported that Surveillance Commissioner Chen Ying had taken gold from the Yan mansion and plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 詔逮瑛，安置廣西，而遷宗山東按察使。

translations.literal: An edict arrested Ying and sent him to settle in Guangxi, while Zong was transferred to Shandong Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An edict arrested Ying and exiled him to Guangxi; Zong became Shandong Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 坐事，左遷刑部郎中，出知蘇州府。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to Director in the Ministry of Punishments and sent out as prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was demoted to Punishments director, then made prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 蘇連歲水，民流，逋租百余萬石。

translations.literal: Suzhou had floods several years running; the people fled and more than a million piculs of grain tax were in arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou flooded several years; people fled and over a million piculs of tax were owed.

sentences.zh: 宗諭富民出米代輸。

translations.literal: Zong instructed the wealthy to provide grain in substitution for payment.
translations.idiomatic: Zong told the wealthy to pay grain on others' behalf.

sentences.zh: 富民知其愛民，不三月悉完納。

translations.literal: The wealthy, knowing he loved the people, completed payment within three months.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he loved the people, the wealthy paid in full within three months.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，有言其坐視水患者，逮下獄，謫判祿州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle someone said he had sat by while waterworks failed; he was arrested, imprisoned, and demoted to judge of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1 someone accused him of neglecting flood control; he was arrested, imprisoned, and demoted to judge of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 以黃淮薦，召為大理寺丞。

translations.literal: On Huang Huai's recommendation he was summoned as Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: On Huang Huai's recommendation he was summoned as Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 或言宗曾發潛邸事。

translations.literal: Some said Zong had once revealed matters of the hidden residence.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Zong had once revealed affairs of the prince's hidden residence.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「帝王惟才是使，何論舊嫌。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Emperors employ only talent—why dwell on old grievances?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Emperors use men for their ability—why dwell on old grievances?"

sentences.zh: 時外國貢使病死，從人謂醫殺之。

translations.literal: At the time a foreign tribute envoy died of illness, and his attendants said the doctor had killed him.
translations.idiomatic: A foreign tribute envoy died of illness, and his attendants claimed the doctor had murdered him.

sentences.zh: 獄具，宗閱牘嘆曰：「醫與使者何仇，而故殺之乎？」

translations.literal: When the case was complete, Zong read the file and sighed: "What grudge did the doctor have against the envoy that he would kill him deliberately?"
translations.idiomatic: When the case was complete, Zong read the file and sighed: "What grudge did the doctor have against the envoy that he would kill him deliberately?"

sentences.zh: 卒辨出之。

translations.literal: In the end he vindicated the doctor.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he cleared the doctor.

sentences.zh: 尋命振饑河南，還署戶部事。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to relieve famine in Henan, then returned to handle Revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to relieve famine in Henan, then returned to handle Revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 解縉下獄，詞連宗，坐系十餘年。

translations.literal: When Xie Jin was imprisoned, the testimony implicated Zong, and he was held more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Jin was imprisoned, the testimony implicated Zong, and he was held more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，復官，再遷南京大理卿。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor took the throne, Zong was restored and again promoted to Nanjing Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong Emperor succeeded, Zong was restored and again made Nanjing Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初，清軍山東。

translations.literal: Early in the Xuande reign he inspected troops in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuande reign he inspected troops in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 會天久不雨，極陳民間饑困狀。

translations.literal: As drought lasted long, he urgently described the people's hunger and distress.
translations.idiomatic: As drought dragged on, he urgently described the people's hunger and distress.

sentences.zh: 帝為蠲租免役，罷不急之務。

translations.literal: The emperor remitted taxes, exempted labor service, and suspended non-urgent tasks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remitted taxes, exempted labor service, and suspended non-urgent tasks.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xuande 2.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：永、宣之際，嚴飭吏治，職事修舉。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: In the Yongle and Xuande period, official discipline was strict and duties were well performed.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser says: In the Yongle and Xuande eras, officials were disciplined and duties well performed.

sentences.zh: 若郁新之理賦，楊砥之馬政，劉季篪、虞謙之治獄，可謂能其官矣。

translations.literal: If Yu Xin in managing revenue, Yang Di in horse administration, and Liu Jichi and Yu Qian in judging cases may be said to have fulfilled their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xin in revenue, Yang Di in horse administration, and Liu Jichi and Yu Qian in justice fulfilled their offices.

sentences.zh: 李慶、師逵諸人，清介有執，皆列卿之良也。

translations.literal: Li Qing, Shi Kui, and the others, pure and principled, were all fine among ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qing, Shi Kui, and the like, pure and principled, were exemplary ministers.

sentences.zh: 陳壽、馬京遭讒早廢，惜乎未竟其用。

translations.literal: Chen Shou and Ma Jing met slander and were cast out early—a pity they did not fulfill their use.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou and Ma Jing were slandered and cast aside early—pity their talents were wasted.

sentences.zh: 金忠奮身卒伍，進自藝術末流，而有士君子之行。

translations.literal: Jin Zhong rose from the ranks of soldiers, advanced from the lowest arts, yet had the conduct of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhong rose from the ranks and the diviner's trade, yet lived as a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 當其侃侃持論於文皇父子間，忠直不撓，卒以誠信悟主，豈不偉哉。

translations.literal: When he spoke forthrightly between the Wen Emperor and his son, loyal and straight without yielding, and in the end moved his lord through sincerity—was that not magnificent?
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke plainly between the Yongle Emperor and his son, unbending in loyalty, and won his lord by sincerity—was that not magnificent?
